subsystems.name: Ribbon
subsystems.role: the load-bearing cable itself, a thin flat tape rather than a round rope so it can survive small punctures.
parts: tapered cross-section, thickest at geostationary altitude

subsystems.name: Counterweight
subsystems.role: sits beyond geostationary orbit and holds the ribbon taut through centrifugal effects.

subsystems.name: Anchor and base station
subsystems.role: ties the ribbon to Earth near the equator and handles payload transfer.
parts: ocean platform or equatorial ground site

subsystems.name: Climbers
subsystems.role: robotic cars that grip the ribbon and haul payload upward.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: drives the climbers; nothing can carry fuel for a multi-day climb.

subsystems.name: Tracking and protection
subsystems.role: keeps the ribbon from being cut.

buildSteps.title: Grow the fibre
buildSteps.detail: Carbon nanotubes are grown in a reactor and spun into continuous fibre — the current bottleneck, since individual tubes are strong but the spun yarn is not.

buildSteps.title: Weave the seed ribbon
buildSteps.detail: The fibre is bonded into a ribbon a few centimetres wide and microns thick, with a taper profile that is thickest near geostationary altitude.

buildSteps.title: Deploy a seed cable from orbit
buildSteps.detail: A spacecraft in geostationary orbit unspools ribbon both upward toward the counterweight and downward toward Earth, the lower end being the harder half.

buildSteps.title: Attach the counterweight
buildSteps.detail: Mass is added or captured beyond geostationary orbit until the system's centre of mass sits at geostationary altitude and the lower end hangs under tension.

buildSteps.title: Anchor at the equator
buildSteps.detail: The descending end is secured to a mobile platform on the equator, where weather, shipping and airspace can be managed.

buildSteps.title: Thicken the ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Climbers ferry up extra strands and weave them in until the ribbon can carry useful payloads — a decades-long build-out.

buildSteps.title: Commission climbers
buildSteps.detail: Solar- or laser-powered climbers crawl up at roughly a few hundred kilometres per hour, taking days to reach geostationary altitude.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Continuous debris tracking, ribbon inspection, and repair or replacement of damaged sections.

prerequisites.tech: Macroscale carbon-nanotube fibre of ~50 GPa specific strength
prerequisites.why: individual nanotubes are strong enough on paper, but fibres made from them today are more than an order of magnitude short of the requirement.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, reliable access to geostationary orbit
prerequisites.why: the seed deployment and thousands of tonnes of counterweight still have to be launched conventionally.

prerequisites.tech: High-power laser or microwave power beaming
prerequisites.why: demonstrated at kilowatt scale; climbers need sustained delivery over tens of thousands of kilometres of travel.

prerequisites.tech: Space debris tracking and collision avoidance
prerequisites.why: orbital debris at low altitude could sever a ribbon that crosses those altitudes.

prerequisites.tech: Long-duration materials testing in vacuum and radiation
prerequisites.why: atomic oxygen and micrometeoroids erode thin structures over the years a ribbon must survive.

pathway.milestone: laboratory nanotube fibres in the low single-digit GPa range, plus ongoing concept studies by space-elevator research groups
pathway.unlocks: measurable targets for fibre strength and taper design.

pathway.milestone: kilometre-scale tethers tested in low Earth orbit using conventional high-strength fibres
pathway.unlocks: real data on deployment, orbital dynamics and debris damage.

pathway.milestone: a partial elevator — a ribbon hanging only partway down from geostationary orbit, or a lunar elevator where existing fibres are strong enough
pathway.unlocks: a working cargo-lift system without needing the full Earth-to-surface strength.

pathway.milestone: a full Earth-to-geostationary ribbon carrying routine payloads, as proposed in concept studies by a Japanese construction firm targeting 2050
pathway.unlocks: very low-cost access to orbit and to beyond, if the fibre problem is ever solved.
